outcome: The general problem (find the minimal forbidden induced subgraphs characterizing all word-representable graphs) remains open, but several restricted cases have been fully settled since 26 January 2024: word-representable split graphs, co-bipartite graphs, K_m-K_n (complete bipartite) graphs with a small side, and near-triangulations each now have complete forbidden-induced-subgraph characterizations, all obtained by ordinary human mathematical proof with no AI involvement.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet asks for a characterisation of word-representable graphs (a hereditary class defined via semi-transitive orientations) by minimal forbidden induced subgraphs, in general. This general problem is still explicitly open: the current live Wikipedia article on word-representable graphs (checked 2026-09) still lists exactly this sentence as an open problem, and no source found states or implies the general question has been answered. However, since the frozen revision (26 Jan 2024) a cluster of papers has settled the analogous question for successively larger restricted classes, each a genuine restriction (case) of the stated problem rather than a variant: (1) arXiv:2507.08483 (Roy & Hariharasubramanian, submitted 11 Jul 2025) gives a minimal forbidden induced subgraph characterization of word-representable split graphs with an independent set of size 4, explicitly answering an open question posed by Kitaev and Pyatkin; (2) arXiv:2512.12259 (Srinivasan & Hariharasubramanian, Dec 2025) gives a complete forbidden induced subgraph characterization of word-representable split graphs generally, via a new 'I-circular property' on matrices; (3) arXiv:2512.12274 (same authors, Dec 2025) does the analogous thing for co-bipartite graphs; (4) arXiv:2508.15177 (Chen, Hameed, Kitaev, Aug 2025) characterizes word-representability of K_m-K_n graphs when the smaller side has size at most 4; (5) arXiv:2605.25733 (Roy & Hariharasubramanian, May 2026) gives a complete forbidden-induced-subgraph characterization of word-representable near-triangulations, unifying and correcting earlier partial results and exhibiting a new minimal non-word-representable graph on 7 vertices. I opened and read all six papers the triage found (including arXiv:2502.06979 on minimal forbidden induced subgraphs relating word-representable and comparability graphs, Kenkireth/Sajith/Sasidharan, Feb 2025). None mentions any AI, machine learning, or LLM tool; all are proved by direct combinatorial/matrix-theoretic argument. A search result referenced a 2019 paper (arXiv:1909.09471, well before the window) that used a 'computational' (brute-force, non-AI) characterization for split graphs with clique size 5 — that predates the frozen revision and is unrelated to AI in any case, so it is noted here only to rule it out. Net: the problem is `partial` because genuine sub-cases have been fully settled since the window opened, each in the 'confirmed' direction (a characterization was found, matching the expectation that such classes admit finite forbidden-subgraph characterizations), with `ai_role` none throughout — this appears to be an active but entirely human research programme (much of it out of IIT Guwahati) with no AI contribution found anywhere in it.
competing_reading: One could argue each restricted-class paper (split graphs, co-bipartite graphs, K_m-K_n, near-triangulations) is a 'related problem' rather than a 'case' of the stated problem, since the stated bullet asks for a characterization of word-representable graphs in general and these papers work within proper hereditary subclasses rather than removing territory from the general class. But per §3.1 a case is what you get by restricting the stated question to a class of objects, which is exactly what split graphs, co-bipartite graphs, etc. are (subclasses of general graphs), so I classify these as genuine cases/partial progress rather than variants. The general characterization itself is unambiguously still open.
what_would_settle_it: A paper (or Wikipedia edit) explicitly claiming a complete minimal-forbidden-induced-subgraph characterization for word-representable graphs in general (not restricted to any subclass) would move this to resolved/claimed. Absent that, continued accumulation of solved subclasses keeps it at partial.
